exchanges.author: c_ben
exchanges.subject: Review requested: #1496 (hotfix)
exchanges.body:
Hotfix for the duplicates. Can someone approve fast? No time for tests.

```diff
+++ billing/emit.py
 def finalize_invoice(invoice, endpoints, outbox):
+    if any(e["invoice_id"] == invoice["id"] for e in outbox.events):
+        return
     for url in endpoints:
         outbox.add(invoice["id"], "webhook", url)
+++ migrations/0042_dedupe.py
+def upgrade():
+    op.create_index("outbound_events_dedupe", "outbound_events", ["invoice_id", "kind", "target"], unique=True)
```

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Thanks for jumping on it, but I don't think we should merge this. (1) The any() check then add is check-then-act: two workers handling the same redelivered task both see nothing and both send, which is exactly what happened at 10:04 (14 of the 41 were parallel). (2) The migration builds the unique index without CONCURRENTLY, which locks outbound_events (~40 writes/s) for the whole build, and it will fail anyway because the 41 duplicate rows already exist. #1497 (opened yesterday) does this properly: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on a unique key, deletes existing duplicates, then CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in an autocommit block, with a parallel test. Marcus, can we take #1497 as the emergency change?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Merged #1497 (CI green, Marcus's approval as emergency change under INC-0412). Migration 0042 ran at 14:52: removed 107 duplicate rows (41 emails + 66 webhooks), unique index built concurrently and valid. Before the 18:00 cutoff.

versions.author: worker

prompt: design a webhook delivery service (at-least-once, retries, per-tenant rate limits)

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Scorecard: candidate K., system design (Jordan Ilic, 11/4)

Recommendation: lean hire (senior), pending the coding and behavioral loops.
Requirements and communication: strong. Clarified ordering, payload size and tenant isolation; structured and receptive to feedback.
Design: solid core (queue, workers, backoff with jitter, Postgres outbox, partitioning).
Gaps: idempotency and noisy-neighbor fairness only after prompting; no observability or dead-letter handling unprompted. For a senior bar these matter; probe operational depth in the next loop.
Written from my own notes before reading other feedback.
